prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for the concept and first demonstration of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity (PROTACs)

statement.case_for: Both parts rest on a clear chemical principle that can be stated in one sentence to a broad audience, and both are generative in the sense I care about. Base editing is direct nucleobase chemistry (an engineered deaminase tethered to a programmable nickase) that gives a new capability, single-nucleotide change without a double-strand break, and it has been replicated widely and has entered the clinic. Targeted protein degradation replaces occupancy-driven inhibition with event-driven removal of the target by recruiting an E3 ligase, which is a real conceptual shift that opens previously undruggable targets. Pairing them gives two distinct, non-overlapping achievements, each with a defensible and small set of names: Liu alone for base editing, and Crews and Deshaies, who conceived and first demonstrated PROTACs in 2001, for degradation.
statement.case_against: The two parts are both chemical biology with a medicine flavour, so the committee could be accused of drifting from core chemistry and of rewarding promise over proven therapeutic outcome: no degrader drug is approved and base-editing therapies are early. The three-name cap forces painful omissions (Komor and Gaudelli, Nishida and Kondo, Ciulli, Handa, Ito), and the 2020 CRISPR prize makes base editing look like a derivative of recognised work. A prize on Buchwald-Hartwig or on lipid nanoparticles would rest on more mature, more clearly chemical evidence.

responses.point: Buchwald-Hartwig C-N coupling is the cleanest two-person prize, mature, overwhelmingly adopted, and a classic enabling method, with Kosugi as a precedent.
responses.response: I agree that B002 has the cleanest attribution of anything on the list and a very strong maturity record, and I take seriously that it is arguably overdue. My hesitation is that it is a refinement of a reaction class already honoured in 2010, and I want you to say what the new principle is beyond ligand optimisation, since the ligand-controlled catalytic cycle is where the novelty lies. If you can make that case I would move it into my configuration; at present I hold it outside my top set but it is not far from it.

responses.point: Targeted degradation is a genuinely new pharmacological principle, and a configuration covering both PROTACs and molecular glues (Crews, Deshaies, Handa) fits the standard of something completely new.
responses.response: I share your view of the principle, but I would keep the citation to PROTACs and induced proximity rather than adding Handa, because the cereblon and thalidomide glue story is a separate mechanism-of-action discovery and would stretch one citation across two achievements and four or more people. If the committee wants the glue branch, it should be argued as its own part, not folded in. I also note your own reservation that no degrader is yet approved, which I think is the strongest argument for timing caution.

responses.point: Base editing is chemically precise and mechanistically transparent, with Liu as the driver and Komor and Gaudelli as lead experimentalists, and the work has been reproduced in animals and in the clinic.
responses.response: I agree on the science, and on the point that Nishida and Kondo make full credit ambiguous. Where I differ is that I would not name Komor and Gaudelli: they were the decisive first authors but within Liu's programme, and a Liu-only part is the most defensible and leaves room for the second part. I would also like us to keep prime editing outside this citation so that we separate the original discovery from its later extensions.

responses.point: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry for siRNA and mRNA medicines, with Cullis, Hope and Madden as the core formulation inventors.
responses.response: This is the strongest competitor to my second part in terms of demonstrated impact, since Onpattro and the mRNA vaccines are proven at population scale. I am held back by the diffuse credit (Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer) and by the 2023 Medicine prize overlap, which you and Johan both flag. I keep B016 as my first alternative and would support it if the committee finds a clean three-person subset.

uncertainties: Whether the prime-editing extension (B028) belongs in the base-editing citation or stays separate.
Whether Nishida and Kondo's earlier deaminase-fusion work is a priority claim serious enough to alter a Liu-only part.
Whether the absence of an approved PROTAC drug makes B018 premature and B016 or B002 a safer second part.
Whether two chemical-biology parts is the right balance, or the committee should prefer a more mature core-chemistry achievement such as B002.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I share a Lund affiliation with committee colleagues Peter Somfai and Emma Sparr, but none of the shortlisted candidates appears connected to Lund or to me personally.
